challenges.title: A/B update with rollback
challenges.prompt: Complete the toy A/B bootloader: after install(), boot() should commit the pending slot when healthy, otherwise count failed tries and roll back to the active slot after MAX_TRIES (discarding the pending image). Print the sequence for a bad v2 update followed by a good v3.
challenges.starter:
class ABBoot:
    """Toy bootloader state for an A/B OTA scheme with a boot counter."""
    MAX_TRIES = 3

    def __init__(self):
        self.slots = {"A": "v1", "B": None}
        self.active = "A"
        self.pending = None       # slot being trialled after an update
        self.tries = 0

    def install(self, version):
        inactive = "B" if self.active == "A" else "A"
        self.slots[inactive] = version
        self.pending = inactive
        self.tries = 0
        return inactive

    def boot(self, healthy):
        """Simulate one boot of the pending slot (or the active one if nothing is pending).
        Healthy: commit the pending slot as active. Unhealthy: count the try; after MAX_TRIES
        roll back to the active slot and discard the pending one. Return a status string."""
        return ""

b = ABBoot()
b.install("v2")
for h in [False, False, False]:
    print(b.boot(h))
print(b.boot(True))
b.install("v3")
print(b.boot(True))
print(b.boot(True))
challenges.expected:
boot failed 1x -> retry B
boot failed 2x -> retry B
boot failed 3x -> rollback to A (v1)
boot A (v1)
boot B (v3) -> committed
boot B (v3)
challenges.solution:
class ABBoot:
    """Toy bootloader state for an A/B OTA scheme with a boot counter."""
    MAX_TRIES = 3

    def __init__(self):
        self.slots = {"A": "v1", "B": None}
        self.active = "A"
        self.pending = None       # slot being trialled after an update
        self.tries = 0

    def install(self, version):
        inactive = "B" if self.active == "A" else "A"
        self.slots[inactive] = version
        self.pending = inactive
        self.tries = 0
        return inactive

    def boot(self, healthy):
        """Simulate one boot. `healthy` says whether the new software comes up fine."""
        if self.pending is None:
            return f"boot {self.active} ({self.slots[self.active]})"
        if healthy:
            self.active, self.pending = self.pending, None
            return f"boot {self.active} ({self.slots[self.active]}) -> committed"
        self.tries += 1
        if self.tries >= self.MAX_TRIES:
            bad = self.pending
            self.pending = None
            self.slots[bad] = None
            return f"boot failed {self.tries}x -> rollback to {self.active} ({self.slots[self.active]})"
        return f"boot failed {self.tries}x -> retry {self.pending}"

b = ABBoot()
b.install("v2")
for h in [False, False, False]:
    print(b.boot(h))
print(b.boot(True))
b.install("v3")
print(b.boot(True))
print(b.boot(True))
challenges.explain: The active slot is never overwritten, so a failed update falls back to a known-good image. Real systems (RAUC, SWUpdate, Mender with U-Boot boot counts) implement the same idea. This is a teaching model. Verified by running the solution.

challenges.title: Match device tree nodes to drivers
challenges.prompt: Implement match(node): skip nodes whose status is not okay, then walk the node's compatible list in order (most specific first) and return the first driver whose table contains one of the strings, along with the matching string.
challenges.expected:
serial@4000 -> imx-uart (via fsl,imx6q-uart)
serial@5000 -> ns16550 (via ns16550a)
leds -> no driver bound
mystery@9000 -> no driver bound
challenges.explain: The driver core binds a driver by compatible string, preferring the earliest (most specific) entry, so serial@5000 binds to ns16550 via its fallback string. Disabled or unknown nodes bind nothing. This models the idea, not the kernel's actual code. Verified by running the solution.
